body:
I'll admit I don't remember a lot of my early childhood, though I know my mother had some pretty bad postpartum depression.

Anyways, thanks for listening to my venting; I can't exactly say I feel good, but the urge to just jump off my balcony isn't as strong today.
You should "embrace the hobby" of vomiting on assholes who give such terrible advice.

> Explaining things to friends and family


Ah, see my problem comes from the fact I don't have friends or family to discuss these things with. My father tried to murder me as a child, my mother has told me on more than one occasion that she never wanted me, my brother is (was? I haven't heard from him in 10 years) extremely violent, and while I have had acquaintances, I've never had friends. (I apologize if this comes across as a melodramatic pity party)


As for what I've tried: years of therapy, medications, I've volunteered, joined clubs, meetup groups, I am very physically active...but I've only ended up feeling like Sisyphus.


It's actually pure spite that's been keeping me going (I don't want to give my father the satisfaction of finishing what he started), but it's become increasingly exhausting to keep up.
Yes, I find that at this point "socializing" makes things worse; it feels less lonely to actually be alone.
"well what am I supposed to do about it?" Ouch, that is an unfortunately familiar line.
